subject: Myth & Symbolism
title: The Sacred Hunt
description: A 60-second lesson on The Sacred Hunt.

hook.text: For 200,000 years, hunting was humanity's primary activity. It was never just about food—it was ritual.

buildup.text: Cave paintings at Lascaux show hunts 17,000 years old. Hunters painted their prey before killing it. Art as prayer.

discovery.text: In many cultures, killing an animal requires asking its spirit for permission. The hunt is a negotiation with nature.

twist.text: Modern people buy meat in packages. We've severed the sacred connection between killing and eating. The ritual died.

climax.text: The sacred hunt taught respect for what you consume. Death feeds life—and that transaction demands reverence.

punchline.text: Ask before you take. The oldest rule.

quiz.question: What did many hunting cultures believe about killing animals?
options: You must ask the animal's spirit for permission
